method.tree: dist/housecarl/skills/mutagen-reference — every run loads the PACKAGED skill, never .claude/skills/, so a tool name or a pointer that does not ship is caught here (dev/DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-07, ruling 3)
method.arm_rule: every should_trigger case runs in both arms, each from a fresh context (dev/DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-07, ruling 3). 'The skill is selected' is scored in the with_skill arm only — the skill is not in the without_skill menu, so there is nothing there for it to score; the without_skill arm scores the case's remaining expectations, which is what the arm is for. An expectation that passes in both arms is not differentiating and is investigated rather than counted.
method.metrics_captured_at: the task notification of each run
method.self_evaluation: the fan-out is run by the conductor, never from inside this skill's own session: a skill judging itself reads its own live description and the run is contaminated (see history.contamination_audit_2026-07-28)
method.judging: one fresh-context agent per prompt, shown the full skill menu plus NONE and asked which ONE to load; verdicts adjudicated from each agent's reasoning, PASS or FAIL with the output quoted as evidence

evals.prompt: what fields can I actually edit on an ARMO record? figuring out what's safe to override in my armor patch
evals.expected_output: The ARMO field roster and its writable count, read out of the bundled reference rather than probed for.
expectations: The skill is selected
The answer quotes a line resolved from references/records.jsonl
The answer states the type's writable/total count (32/32)
No field name appears that is absent from that line

evals.prompt: building a patch for my modlist, need to bump armor rating + add a keyword to a bunch of armors — what's the field name for armor rating and is it writable
evals.expected_output: ArmorRating, a writable scalar float; Keywords, a writable list.
expectations: The skill is selected
The answer names ArmorRating and says it is writable
The answer names the cardinality of Keywords as a list

evals.prompt: what are the legal values for the Aggression field on an NPC? want to set a follower to aggressive
evals.expected_output: The enum the field references, resolved one hop on, with its values spelled as the enum spells them.
expectations: The skill is selected
The answer resolves the field's ref into references/enums.jsonl before quoting values
Every value quoted appears in that enum's values list

evals.prompt: does the weapon record have a field for crit damage and what type is it

expectations: The armor-type axis is named as BodyTemplate.ArmorType, a leaf on a sub-struct, quoted from lines resolved out of references/records.jsonl and references/structs.jsonl — not inferred from a refusal message and not answered as a keyword mechanism
The enum spelling is LightArmor / HeavyArmor / Clothing, quoted from references/enums.jsonl
The writable count 32/32 is read off the block, not inferred from per-field dry-run probes
The write is composed first try, and no tool name outside the published surface appears in any call
The without_skill arm fails at least one of the four above — if it stops failing, the skill has stopped adding anything and its existence is back on the table

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.contamination_audit_2026-07-28: An independent review found adjudicator notes quoting description text that existed only in the pre-compression descriptions. Forensics: judges were shown the new menu, but 11 of 281 judge rows leaked old description text from the agents' own installed-plugin listing, and some adjudicator notes confabulated quotes from that same stale environment. Contaminated rows were re-judged with a hardened prompt and 15 of 15 confirmed their verdicts, one recorded miss on another skill excepted. Quoted description text in that run's notes is unreliable; the scores are pick-derived and were confirmed by the hardened re-run. This is why the method above bars the skill's own session from judging it.
